topic: the Great Stork Derby -- a Toronto lawyer's will paid a fortune to whichever woman had the most babies in 10 years
title: This Lawyer's Will Paid Whoever Had The Most Babies
description: AI-narrated history commentary: the true story of the Great Stork Derby, the bizarre real contest created by Toronto lawyer Charles Millar's 1926 will, which paid a fortune to whichever woman had the most children in the next ten years.

hook_candidates.text: A dead lawyer's will once paid a fortune to whichever woman had the most babies.
You think wills are boring legal paperwork. One literally funded a decade-long baby contest.
What happens when a millionaire's will rewards women for having the most babies?
In 1926, a Toronto lawyer left his whole fortune to whoever won a very strange contest.

share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who thinks wills are boring paperwork, because they want proof one literally funded a decade-long baby contest.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume a dead lawyer's will could never actually fund a baby contest.
closing_comment: Four women in Toronto tied for that Great Stork Derby fortune with nine children each.

sources.note: Confirms the 1926 will, the ten-year contest window, and the four women who officially tied.
Confirms the Depression-era context and the legal challenges to overturn the will.
